title: Allowing public ACLs or policies on a S3 bucket is security-sensitive
description: Allowing public ACLs or policies on an Amazon S3 bucket can expose sensitive data to unauthorized users. S3 buckets are used to store data in the cloud, and improper configuration of access control lists (ACLs) or bucket policies can make the data publicly accessible. This is a security-sensitive operation that can lead to data breaches, compliance violations, and unauthorized access to critical information.
message: Make sure that granting public access to this S3 bucket is safe here.
recommendation: Ensure that S3 buckets are not publicly accessible unless explicitly required. Use private ACLs and bucket policies, implement proper IAM policies, and regularly audit bucket permissions.

references.name: OWASP Top 10 2021 - A01 Broken Access Control

noncompliant.code:
import boto3

s3 = boto3.client('s3')

# Noncompliant: Setting bucket ACL to public-read
s3.put_bucket_acl(
    Bucket='my-bucket',
    ACL='public-read'
)

# Noncompliant: Setting bucket ACL to public-read-write
s3.put_bucket_acl(
    Bucket='my-bucket',
    ACL='public-read-write'
)

# Noncompliant: Creating bucket with public ACL
s3.create_bucket(
    Bucket='my-bucket',
    ACL='public-read'
)

# Noncompliant: Bucket policy allowing public access
public_policy = {
    'Version': '2012-10-17',
    'Statement': [{
        'Effect': 'Allow',
        'Principal': '*',
        'Action': 's3:GetObject',
        'Resource': 'arn:aws:s3:::my-bucket/*'
    }]
}
s3.put_bucket_policy(
    Bucket='my-bucket',
    Policy=json.dumps(public_policy)
)

compliant.code:
import boto3
import json

s3 = boto3.client('s3')

# Compliant: Using private ACL (default)
s3.put_bucket_acl(
    Bucket='my-bucket',
    ACL='private'
)

# Compliant: Creating bucket without public ACL
s3.create_bucket(
    Bucket='my-bucket'
)

# Compliant: Bucket policy with specific principal
restricted_policy = {
    'Version': '2012-10-17',
    'Statement': [{
        'Effect': 'Allow',
        'Principal': {'AWS': 'arn:aws:iam::123456789012:user/specific-user'},
        'Action': 's3:GetObject',
        'Resource': 'arn:aws:s3:::my-bucket/*'
    }]
}
s3.put_bucket_policy(
    Bucket='my-bucket',
    Policy=json.dumps(restricted_policy)
)

# Compliant: Blocking public access
s3.put_public_access_block(
    Bucket='my-bucket',
    PublicAccessBlockConfiguration={
        'BlockPublicAcls': True,
        'IgnorePublicAcls': True,
        'BlockPublicPolicy': True,
        'RestrictPublicBuckets': True
    }
)

why_is_this_an_issue: Making S3 buckets publicly accessible can lead to serious security vulnerabilities. When ACLs or bucket policies are configured to allow public access, any user on the internet can potentially access, read, or even modify the data stored in the bucket. This can result in data breaches, exposure of sensitive information, compliance violations, and unauthorized data manipulation. Even if the data seems non-sensitive, public buckets can be used for malicious purposes such as hosting malware or conducting DDoS attacks at the bucket owner's expense.
how_to_fix: Remove public ACLs: Use 'private' ACL instead of 'public-read' or 'public-read-write'
Restrict bucket policies: Replace wildcard principals ('*') with specific AWS account IDs or IAM users
Enable S3 Block Public Access: Use put_public_access_block to prevent accidental public access
Implement least privilege: Grant only the minimum necessary permissions to specific users or services
Regular auditing: Periodically review bucket permissions and access patterns
Use pre-signed URLs: For temporary public access, use pre-signed URLs instead of making buckets public
